claim: does the closed-loop PLL (design/top/top.sch -- VCO + PFD/charge pump + loop filter + divider, issue #28), driven from a cold start (RESETB power-on, VCTRL starting at whatever the loop filter's own initial condition is) with a 25 MHz reference (spec/target-spec.md row 3's DRAFT high band edge), lock its output to N * Fref = 10 * 25 MHz = 250 MHz within this manifest's transient window -- issue #55's sibling of sim/pll-lock's own 10 MHz-reference campaign, exercising row 3's frequency-range claim at more than the single 10 MHz point sim/pll-lock/testbench/tb_pll_lock.sch drives. This is a design-input record, not a spec claim: row 3 is DRAFT/unratified. 250 MHz is deliberately the same target frequency sim/pll-lock/testbench/tb_pll_lock.sch already targets (N=25 * 10 MHz), so this record is directly comparable to that one -- only the reference frequency (and, by construction, N) changes.
methodology_note: this testbench's DUT is design/top/top.sch, the real four-block closed-loop PLL (not a throwaway circuit) -- straps NSEL[5:0]=001001 (N=10) and drives REF with a 25 MHz clock and RESETB with the same power-on reset pwl sim/pll-lock/testbench/tb_pll_lock.sch uses. N=10 was chosen (see sim/pll-lock-25mhz/testbench/tb_pll_lock_25mhz.sch's header comment for the arithmetic) to land the closed-loop target inside sim/vco/records/20260819-131741-fe0e6df.md's characterized VCO tuning range (~145.1 MHz to ~1.034 GHz) at exactly the same 250 MHz target sim/pll-lock/testbench/tb_pll_lock.sch already exercises with N=25 at a 10 MHz reference -- so a difference in outcome between this record and that one isolates the effect of the reference frequency (loop update rate) rather than a different target output frequency. `require_lock` is false, for the same reason sim/pll-lock's own manifest gives: a point that completes but never locks is recorded as evidence, not a harness failure. A gated pass/fail, and any resulting spec/design decision, is deferred to a future ratifying DR once this record and sim/pll-lock's own are both available to argue from. process_corners is the ratified rows 19/20 PVT grid (spec/target-spec.md, DR-003, #77) -- sky130's five standard MOS/BJT process corners including the two mixed-skew corners (sf, fs) that stress this design's un-cascoded PFD/charge-pump UP/DN current mirror -- not a bare local convention, following sim/pll's own tb.json (PR #86); this supersedes the tt/ss/ff-only grid this manifest originally declared (issue #52).
